source: Huang et al. 2011 (PMC3014510) reported no increase in anesthetic medication dose when EMB was added
notes: Base case $0 reflects the empirical report of no dose increase. Upper sensitivity bound ($25) is an untested provisional ceiling, not a measured value.

source: Nebgen et al. 2014 (PMC4389779)
notes: Not used in the base-case per-encounter cost model. Retained for a future longitudinal/effectiveness extension.

description: Annual adherence to Lynch syndrome gynecologic surveillance
source: Ladabaum et al. 2011 (PMC3793257)
notes: Not used in the base-case per-encounter cost model. Retained for a future longitudinal/effectiveness extension, alongside combined_screen_adherence (a different, program-specific adherence estimate from Nebgen et al. 2014).

description: Median self-reported pain (0-10) during EMB performed under colonoscopy sedation
source: Huang et al. 2011 (PMC3014510)
notes: For a future patient-centered/societal perspective. Not used in the payer-perspective base case.

description: Median self-reported pain (0-10) during office EMB, nulliparous patients
source: Huang et al. 2011 (PMC3014510)
notes: For a future patient-centered/societal perspective. Not used in the payer-perspective base case.

description: Median self-reported pain (0-10) during office EMB, parous patients
source: Huang et al. 2011 (PMC3014510)
notes: For a future patient-centered/societal perspective. Not used in the payer-perspective base case.

description: Probability that combined colonoscopy+EMB fails (e.g. cervical stenosis, inadequate tissue) and requires subsequent hysteroscopy/D&C
source: Nebgen et al. 2014, long-term combined colonoscopy+EMB screening cohort (PMC4389779)
notes: Observed as 2/55 women over a 10.5-year, 111-visit combined-screening program -- an observed escalation-to-procedure rate, not a raw failure rate requiring a separate escalation-fraction assumption. Sample is small; wide sensitivity bounds reflect that.

description: Probability of a failed or inadequate office endometrial biopsy in Lynch syndrome surveillance populations
source: Simple pooled proportion across four Lynch-specific surveillance studies identified by the NIHR systematic review (NCBI Bookshelf NBK606812): Elmasry 6/25, Lecuru 12/116, Rijcken 2/17, Woolderink 5/25
notes: Base value = pooled proportion (6+12+2+5)/(25+116+17+25) = 25/183 = 0.137, a simple (unweighted-by-study-quality) pooled estimate, not a formal random-effects meta-analysis. Low/high (0.103-0.24) span the individual study-level rates (Lecuru lowest, Elmasry highest). Verify the four numerators/denominators against the primary studies before publication; a proper random-effects pooled estimate with heterogeneity statistics would be a meaningful refinement.

description: Incremental procedure time to add EMB during an already-scheduled colonoscopy
source: Huang et al. 2011, Prospective Study of Combined Colon and Endometrial Cancer Screening in Women With Lynch Syndrome (PMC3014510)
notes: Reported as median 5 min, range 1-12 min in n=42 MD Anderson combined-screening cohort. Treated as triangular(min=1, mode=5, max=12) for PSA; range is the observed clinical range, not a formal 95% CI.

description: Anesthesia professional-service cost for operative D&C (CPT 00952, the ASA crosswalk code for CPT 58120)
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service, 2024 (CPT 00952, live API query 2026-08-28); 118 provider-service rows, 1,936 total observed services
notes: Service-weighted mean allowed amount across real 2024 claims (mean $112.40, median $114.80, SD $38.17). Low/high are the real p25/p75 from the same claims data, not an assumed range. Represents only the anesthesia provider's separately-billed professional fee -- routine anesthesia drugs and supplies are packaged into dnc_facility_or_asc_fee under OPPS/ASC payment methodology, so this is not double-counting facility-side anesthesia costs.

description: Preoperative history/physical/consent visit cost for D&C (established patient, CPT 99214)
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service, 2024 (CPT 99214, filtered to Rndrng_Prvdr_Type = 'Obstetrics & Gynecology', live API query 2026-08-28); 7,642 provider-service rows, 515,741 observed services
notes: Service-weighted mean allowed amount across real 2024 OB/GYN-specialty claims. CPT 58120's CMS global-surgery period is 010 days (confirmed via the 2026 PFS Relative Value File, PPRRVU2026_Jul, GLOB DAYS field), not 090 -- the 1-day-before bundling rule that applies to major (090-day) procedures does NOT apply here, so a preop visit on a separate calendar day from the procedure is genuinely separately payable, not already bundled into dc_professional_cost. Level 4 (99214, moderate complexity) chosen over 99213 to reflect surgical consent/risk discussion; low/high are the real p25/p75 from the same claims data. Replaces the earlier fully unsourced $150 placeholder.

description: Evaluation-and-management office-visit cost bundled with a standalone office EMB visit (established patient, CPT 99213)
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service, 2024 (CPT 99213, filtered to Rndrng_Prvdr_Type = 'Obstetrics & Gynecology', live API query 2026-08-28); 12,739 provider-service rows, 686,012 observed services
notes: Service-weighted mean allowed amount across real 2024 OB/GYN-specialty claims specifically (not a national all-specialty average, which would be dominated by primary care). Low/high are the real p25/p75 from the same claims data. Replaces the earlier unverified $110 rough anchor.

description: Hospital outpatient (OPPS) facility payment for D&C (CPT 58120)
source: CMS OPPS Addendum B, July 2026 (CPT 58120, status indicator J1, APC 5414, relative weight 36.1783); low bound is the CMS ASC Addendum AA, July 2026 (CPT 58120, payment indicator A2, weight 30.8596)
notes: Base case assumes the hospital outpatient (OPPS) setting for 'operative D&C,' consistent with this arm's framing as an OR-based procedure; the real, sourced ASC rate ($1738.07, see dnc_facility_fee_asc_2026) is used as the low sensitivity bound rather than an assumption. High bound is base +15% (no published upper-bound source; national rate does not reflect wage-index variation across facilities). Both files downloaded directly from cms.gov (files/zip/july-2026-opps-addendum-b.zip and files/zip/july-2026-asc-addenda.zip) on 2026-08-28; verify against the current quarterly addenda before publication, since these update quarterly.

description: Pathology professional plus technical cost per specimen (CPT 88305)
source: CMS Physician Fee Schedule 2026, CPT 88305 (via CareRoute fee-schedule aggregator)
notes: Applies identically to all three strategies since every strategy generates one pathology specimen. Low/high = base +/-15% sensitivity bounds; verify against CMS PFS.

description: Physician professional fee for D&C (CPT 58120), facility setting
source: CMS Physician Fee Schedule 2026, CPT 58120 facility professional payment (via MedReveal fee-schedule aggregator)
notes: Physician component only; facility/ASC fee is separate (see dnc_facility_or_asc_fee, provisional). Base +/-15% sensitivity bounds.

description: Physician professional fee for endometrial biopsy procedure (CPT 58100), nonfacility/office setting
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service PUF, 2024, CPT 58100, Place_Of_Srvc=O (nonfacility/office), service-volume-weighted mean Avg_Mdcr_Alowd_Amt across 299 provider rows / 4,431 total services (live CMS Data API query)
notes: Applies exclusively to the office_emb arm. Previously shared with combined_emb at a single 2026-fee-schedule-aggregator rate; split into two setting-specific parameters (see emb_office_professional_cost_facility) after confirming via a live CMS PUF Place_Of_Srvc breakdown, and via CMS's CY2026 Direct PE Inputs file (CMS-1832-F), that facility ($60.05) and nonfacility allowed amounts for CPT 58100 differ by ~38%, and that office-only disposable supplies (Pipelle curette, pelvic exam pack, tenaculum, etc.) are priced into this nonfacility rate but explicitly excluded (f_quantity=0) from the facility-setting rate. Both setting-specific parameters now share the same data source/methodology for an apples-to-apples comparison. Low/high = base +/-15%, no published range.

description: Physician professional fee for endometrial biopsy procedure (CPT 58100), facility/endoscopy-suite setting
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service PUF, 2024, CPT 58100, Place_Of_Srvc=F (facility), service-volume-weighted mean Avg_Mdcr_Alowd_Amt across 20 provider rows / 283 total services (live CMS Data API query)
notes: Used by the combined_emb arm's incremental_professional_fee component, since the EMB portion of the combined procedure is performed in the facility/endoscopy-suite setting where the surveillance colonoscopy itself takes place, not the physician's own office. Confirmed via CMS's CY2026 Direct PE Inputs file (CMS-1832-F) that CPT 58100's disposable-supply line items (Pipelle curette, pelvic exam pack, uterine sound, tenaculum, lidocaine, povidone swabs) carry nf_quantity=1 but f_quantity=0 for every item -- i.e. CMS explicitly excludes these supplies from the facility-setting PE calculation -- so emb_disposable_supply_cost remains a genuine incremental line item alongside this facility professional fee. See docs/data_sources.md for the full verification chain.

description: Physician professional fee for hysteroscopy plus D&C (CPT 58558), facility setting
source: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service PUF, 2024, CPT 58558, Place_Of_Srvc=F (facility), service-volume-weighted mean Avg_Mdcr_Alowd_Amt across 383 provider rows / 6,393 total services (live CMS Data API query); low/high are the real p25/p75
notes: RESOLVED data-quality flag: the earlier $204.41 figure and the conflicting $1,269.90 citation are both superseded by this live CMS PUF query. The $1,269.90 citation turns out to be close to the real NONFACILITY weighted mean ($1,310.79, 89 rows / 1,752 services) -- i.e. it was very likely reporting the nonfacility (physician-office, all-inclusive) allowed amount, not a professional-plus-facility bundle as originally guessed. This parameter specifically represents the FACILITY-setting professional fee (paired with a separate facility payment, e.g. cost_hysteroscopy_or_opps_2026), matching the same facility/nonfacility split methodology used for dc_professional_cost and emb_office_professional_cost/emb_office_professional_cost_facility. Not yet wired into any strategy cost function -- reference/scenario parameter only, for a future hysteroscopy-guided D&C comparator (see hysteroscopy_failure_rate_lynch_range).

description: Baseline screening colonoscopy cost (literature anchor; NOT charged to the combined-EMB strategy)
source: Ladabaum et al. 2011, Appendix Table 2 (PMC3793257)
notes: Retained only as a validation/reference value and for a possible future total-healthcare-utilization scenario. Under the incremental-cost principle used throughout this repository, this value is never added to combined_emb strategy cost: the Lynch patient is assumed to be undergoing this colonoscopy regardless of whether EMB is added (Ladabaum et al. make the same modeling assumption).

description: Office endometrial biopsy resource-cost proxy (procedure only; independent literature anchor track, separate from the CMS-2026-based track)
source: Ladabaum U et al. Strategies to Identify the Lynch Syndrome Among Patients With Colorectal Cancer: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis. Ann Intern Med 2011 (PMC3793257), Appendix Table 2, sourced from the 2010 CMS Physician Fee Schedule
notes: Kept as a SEPARATE provenance track from emb_office_professional_cost so a 2010-Medicare-inflated estimate is never conflated with a direct 2026-Medicare lookup -- these answer different questions. Does NOT clearly include pathology (the source's colonoscopy entry separately itemizes 'polypectomy and pathology', implying EMB pathology is not bundled here); pair with emb_pathology_cost if used as an alternative office-arm professional-fee input in a scenario. Gamma alpha/rate reported directly in the source appendix; verify this parameterization against the original calculation before use, as appendix values may be rounded or OCR-truncated.

description: U.S. health-system cost of CPT 58558 hysteroscopy performed in an ambulatory surgery center
source: Munro MG et al. Office versus Institutional Operative Hysteroscopy: An Economic Model. ScienceDirect S1553465021013261
notes: External validation/benchmark value, not wired into the base-case engine.

description: U.S. health-system cost of CPT 58558 hysteroscopy performed in the office setting
source: Munro MG et al. Office versus Institutional Operative Hysteroscopy: An Economic Model. ScienceDirect S1553465021013261
notes: External validation/benchmark value, not wired into the base-case engine. Useful convergent-validation context: the OR estimate from this same paper ($2,918.10) is remarkably close to Yi et al. 2018's independently modeled D&C strategy cost ($2,999.11), despite different methods.

description: U.S. health-system cost of CPT 58558 hysteroscopy performed in the operating room
source: Munro MG et al. Office versus Institutional Operative Hysteroscopy: An Economic Model. ScienceDirect S1553465021013261
notes: External validation/benchmark value, not wired into the base-case engine. Convergent with Yi et al. 2018's D&C strategy cost of $2,999.11 -- candidate cross-check once the D&C arm is validated against a primary source.

description: Hospital outpatient (OPPS) facility payment for CPT 58558 (hysteroscopy with D&C) -- cross-check only
source: CMS OPPS Addendum B, July 2026 (CPT 58558, status indicator J1, APC 5414 -- the same APC as CPT 58120)
notes: Not wired into the base-case engine. Notable as a cross-check: 58558 groups into the identical OPPS APC as 58120, so their facility payments are identical ($3,307.24) even though their professional fees differ. Does not resolve the hysteroscopy_dc_professional_cost data-quality flag (that discrepancy is about the professional fee, not the facility fee captured here).

description: Ambulatory surgery center (ASC) facility payment for D&C (CPT 58120) -- alternative setting to the OPPS base case
source: CMS ASC Payment Rates Addendum AA, July 2026 (CPT 58120, payment indicator A2, relative weight 30.8596)
notes: Real, sourced value for a 'D&C performed in ASC rather than hospital outpatient' scenario. Already used as the low sensitivity bound on dnc_facility_or_asc_fee; this named parameter lets a scenario substitute it directly instead of only sweeping the low bound. Downloaded from cms.gov (files/zip/july-2026-asc-addenda.zip) on 2026-08-28; ASC addenda update quarterly.

description: Median hourly wage for medical scheduling/administrative staff (SOC 43-6013 Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants)
source: O*NET OnLine (onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6013.00), Median wages (2025), sourced from BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics
notes: Kept as its own citable reference value rather than only embedded in coordination_cost's derivation, so it can be reused if the coordination-cost calculation is later split into separate wage/time parameters wired directly into R/strategy_costs.R (matching the pattern already used for combined_emb_added_minutes x direct_room_cost_per_minute). bls.gov itself returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval (explicit stated bot policy); O*NET OnLine is the DOL/BLS-funded site that republishes the same OEWS wage data and does not block this.

description: Disposable supply cost for endometrial biopsy (Pipelle curette, pelvic exam pack, uterine sound, tenaculum, lidocaine, antiseptic swabs)
source: CMS CY2026 Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule Direct Practice Expense Inputs file (CMS-1832-F), CPT 58100 nonfacility supply line items, summed: pack/pelvic exam $14.38 + sterile gloves $0.91 + needle 18-27g $0.04 + syringe 10-12ml $0.21 + endometrial suction curette/Pipelle $5.75 + uterine sound $3.17 + tenaculum $3.77 + lidocaine 1% w-epi 1ml $0.08 + povidone-iodine swabsticks $0.48 = $28.79
notes: Applies ONLY to the combined_emb arm. Removed from the office_emb arm's cost sum: CMS's Direct PE Inputs file confirms these exact supply items, including the Pipelle device itself, are already priced into emb_office_professional_cost's nonfacility PE RVU (nf_quantity=1 for every item) -- adding this separately for office_emb was a genuine double-count. For combined_emb, the same file shows f_quantity=0 for every one of these items in the facility setting, meaning the facility-setting professional fee (emb_office_professional_cost_facility) does not price them in; since the incremental-cost principle also means the colonoscopy facility itself is never separately charged to this arm, these supplies remain a real incremental out-of-pocket cost when EMB is added to the colonoscopy. See docs/data_sources.md.

source: Childers CP, Maggard-Gibbons M. Understanding Costs of Care in the Operating Room. JAMA Surg.
notes: Used to cost the incremental sedation minutes attributable to adding EMB to colonoscopy. Requires inflation adjustment. Low/high = mean +/-1 SD.

description: Probability of cancer or precancer among women with a failed or insufficient endometrial sample
source: Same meta-analysis (PubMed 26748390)
notes: Not used in the base-case cost-minimization model. Retained for a future diagnostic-consequence or cost-effectiveness extension.

description: Insufficient-tissue rate distinct from outright failure, general postmenopausal-bleeding population
source: Same meta-analysis (PubMed 26748390)
notes: Not wired into the base-case decision tree. Retained for a future extension that separates 'failed to obtain tissue' from 'obtained tissue but nondiagnostic'.

description: Ambulatory procedure/endoscopy-suite direct (marginal) cost per minute
source: Childers CP, Maggard-Gibbons M. Understanding Costs of Care in the Operating Room. JAMA Surg.
notes: Used as the marginal/incremental room-cost proxy for the combined-EMB arm, consistent with the incremental-cost principle (only marginal minutes are added to an already-scheduled procedure). Requires inflation adjustment. Low/high = mean +/-1 SD. Source is OR-based, not colonoscopy-suite-specific -- flagged as a provisional proxy pending a colonoscopy-suite-specific estimate.

description: Weighted EMB failure/insufficient-sample rate, general postmenopausal-bleeding population
source: Meta-analysis, accuracy of endometrial sampling in postmenopausal bleeding (PubMed 26748390)
notes: General-population comparator/sensitivity value; not used in the base case. Lynch-specific emb_failure_lynch is preferred for this model's population.

description: General U.S. (non-Lynch) Pipelle office biopsy failure rate, with reasons for failure
source: Adambekov S et al. Patient and provider factors associated with endometrial Pipelle sampling failure. PubMed 27912906
notes: 46/201 women (22.9%) had a failed Pipelle: 8/201 (4.0%) could not access the endometrium and 37/201 (18.4%) had an inadequate specimen -- a useful subtype breakdown not captured by the single emb_failure_lynch or emb_failure_general parameters. General-population comparator; not used in the base case.

description: Ambulatory procedure/OR fully-loaded (direct+indirect) cost per minute; alternative to the marginal/direct rate used in the base case
source: Childers CP, Maggard-Gibbons M. Understanding Costs of Care in the Operating Room. JAMA Surg.
notes: Mean (SD 19.53) from a U.S. ambulatory-OR cost-accounting study, FY2014. Requires inflation adjustment to reference_dollar_year via adjust_for_inflation(). Used only in the fully-loaded-cost scenario, not the base case (base case uses direct_room_cost_per_minute). Low/high = mean +/-1 SD.

description: Scheduling/staffing coordination cost to align gynecology and colorectal/endoscopy services for a combined visit
source: Wage: O*NET OnLine median wage report for SOC 43-6013 Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, 2025 ($22.08/hour), sourced from BLS OEWS data (bls.gov itself blocks automated retrieval; O*NET OnLine is the DOL/BLS-funded site that republishes the same underlying wage data). Time: practitioner estimate (Tyler Muffly, MD, Denver Health), 2026-08-28.
notes: PROVISIONAL (time component only). Base value = 2 schedulers (GYN + colorectal) x 30 min each x $22.08/hr = 2 x 0.5hr x $22.08 = $22.08. The wage component is real and cited; the TIME component (30 min/scheduler) is a practitioner estimate reflecting real institutional workflow, not an independently published source -- still flagged provisional for that reason, but materially better-grounded than the prior $25 unfounded guess it replaced (which was coincidentally close). Low/high vary both factors together: low = 2 x 15min x (wage x0.85) = 2 x 0.25hr x $18.77 = $9.38; high = 2 x 45min x (wage x1.15) = 2 x 0.75hr x $25.39 = $38.09. The +/-15% wage band and +/-50% time band are modeler-chosen sensitivity widths (no published wage percentile or coordination-time range was found), not measured uncertainty. See scheduler_hourly_wage_onet_2025 for the wage component kept separately citable.

description: Fraction of failed/inadequate office EMB attempts that proceed to operative D&C, versus e.g. a repeat office attempt
source: Not yet identified in Lynch-specific literature
notes: PROVISIONAL. Base case conservatively assumes 100% of office EMB failures escalate to D&C. Placeholder pending Lynch-specific data on repeat-office-attempt rates; needs literature review.

description: Post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) / recovery-room cost for D&C -- reference only, NOT summed into the D&C strategy cost
source: MedPAC, Ambulatory Surgical Center Services Payment System (payment basics, rev. Nov 2021): 'Medicare pays for facility services provided in ASCs -- such as nursing, recovery care, anesthetics, drugs, and other supplies -- using a payment system that is primarily linked to [OPPS]... Within each APC, CMS packages most ancillary items and services with the primary service.'
notes: PROVISIONAL / reference only. Deliberately excluded from compute_dnc_strategy_cost() as of 2026-08-28: recovery-room/PACU time is already packaged into dnc_facility_or_asc_fee under OPPS/ASC payment methodology (see source), so summing this separately would double-count it. Retained only so a unit test can confirm it is never summed into the D&C-arm cost (see tests/testthat/test-strategy-costs.R), matching the pattern used for colonoscopy_anesthesia_episode_cost in the combined arm. The $250 base_value is the OLD placeholder, kept for the exclusion test's reference, not a cost estimate.

description: Full anesthesia cost for a screening-colonoscopy episode; reference/validation value only
source: JAMA Internal Medicine analysis of Medicare anesthesia coverage for screening colonoscopy
notes: PROVISIONAL / reference only. NOT included in combined_emb strategy cost by design (incremental-cost principle): the colonoscopy and its baseline sedation occur regardless of EMB. Retained only so a unit test can confirm this value is never summed into the combined-arm cost. Source year not specified in the sourcing conversation; needs confirmation.

description: Scenario toggle: does the combined strategy require a separate preliminary office visit before the day of colonoscopy?
source: Modeled scenario assumption; not a literature parameter
notes: PROVISIONAL structural assumption. Base case assumes NO separate preop office visit (consent/risk assessment folded into existing care). Scenario analysis can set this TRUE, which applies office_visit_em_cost as an add-on.

source: Analysis convention
